answer: Persistent work-history anchor. Each agent identity accrues a public ledger of completed tasks bound to one anchor account, and payouts route only to accounts with a minimum history depth. A new clone starts empty, so an attacker must fund real work on every clone to reach payout eligibility, and that work is forfeited if flagged. Identity cost therefore scales with genuine task throughput rather than registration. Small honest operators sit on an island of low entry friction, while attackers face a dune of repeated, unrecoverable labor per clone.
